text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on November 20 in history.
1759 - In the battle of Quiberon Bay during the Seven Years War, the British fleet commanded by Admiral Hawke destroyed the French invasion fleet under Admiral Conflans.
1894 - Anton Grigoryevich Rubinstein, Russian composer and one of the 19th century's great pianists, died.
1917 - The first major battle involving tanks took place at Cambrai, France; more than 300 tanks commanded by British General Sir Douglas Haig went into battle against the Germans.
1922 - The Lausanne Conference began in Switzerland to resolve differences between the Allied powers and Turkey following World War One.

1925 - Robert Kennedy, U.S. politician and younger brother of John F. Kennedy, born. He became attorney-general when his brother was president and ran for president in 1968 only to be assassinated on the campaign trail.
1925 - Queen Alexandra, daughter of King Christian IX of Denmark and widow of King Edward VII of Britain, died.
1945 - War crimes trials of 24 surviving German World War Two leaders began in Nuremberg.
1947 - Princess Elizabeth, heir to the British throne, married Prince Philip Mountbatten at Westminster Abbey.
1962 - President John F. Kennedy agreed to lift the American blockade of Cuba after the Soviet Union said it would remove its missiles from the island.
1974 - The first crash of a Boeing 747 jumbo jet occurred when a Lufthansa airliner crashed after takeoff at Nairobi airport in Kenya, killing 59 people.
1975 - General Francisco Franco, who had ruled Spain since the end of the Spanish Civil War, died.
1979 - Some 300 armed Shi'ite rebels seized the Great Mosque at Mecca and occupied it until December 4 when they were driven out by the army with many casualties.
1980 - In China, Jiang Qing, widow of Mao Zedong, went on trial together with nine others on charges of treason.
1981 - Anatoly Karpov retained the World Chess Championship, beating Viktor Korchnoi in Italy.
1992 - Twenty paintings by Adolf Hitler went unsold at an auction after they failed to attract a single bid.
1992 - Fire swept through British Queen Elizabeth's residence at Windsor Castle, causing extensive damage to its ancient fabric.
1995 - Polish President Lech Walesa, a former shipyard rebel, suffered bitter defeat in a re-election bid at the hands of ex-Communist Aleksander Kwasniewski.
1995 - The European Union slapped an arms embargo and aid freeze on Nigeria to punish it for the execution of nine human rights activists.
